previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with acute chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulder, diagnosed as NSTEMI based on elevated troponin and EKG changes. She underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed severe three-vessel disease. The LAD artery was dilated with balloon angioplasty, but no stent was placed due to her underlying immune thrombocytopenic purpura and platelet count of 80,000. The RCA was chronically occluded and left untreated, and the circumflex could not be engaged due to tortuosity. She was pre-treated for contrast allergy and tolerated the procedure well. Her isosorbide mononitrate was increased to 60 mg daily, and she was started on a one-month course of clopidogrel. She remained stable, with troponin trending down, and was discharged home in good condition with cardiology follow-up planned.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with fall and left hematoma along the gluteal
area.  Evaluate for aortic dissection, bleeding and the left gluteal area.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the chest, abdomen and
pelvis without intravenous contrast administration.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 7.5 s, 82.5 cm; CTDIvol = 13.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,081.6 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 1.1 s, 12.0 cm; CTDIvol = 5.5 mGy (Body) DLP = 66.2
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 1,148 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT from ___.

FINDINGS: 

CHEST:
HEART AND VASCULATURE:  The patient is status post repair of a type A aortic
dissection.  Further evaluation of the dissection is limited due to lack of
intravenous contrast material, though it appears similar to prior exams.  The
heart is normal in size, and coronary artery and aortic valvular
calcifications are noted.  There is no significant pericardial effusion.

AXILLA, HILA, AND MEDIASTINUM: No axillary, mediastinal, or hilar
lymphadenopathy is present.  No mediastinal mass or hematoma.  The patient is
status post left mastectomy.  Right axillary surgical clips are noted.

PLEURAL SPACES: No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  A fat containing right
Bochdalek hernia is noted.

LUNGS/AIRWAYS: Lungs are clear without masses or areas of parenchymal
opacification.  Dependent atelectasis and scarring is noted in the bilateral
lower lobes.  The airways are patent to the level of the segmental bronchi
bilaterally.

BASE OF NECK: Visualized portions of the base of the neck show no acute
abnormality.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesion or laceration.  There is no evidence of
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within
normal limits.

PANCREAS: Fatty atrophy of the pancreas is noted, and there is no evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesion or laceration.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY:  Atrophy of the right kidney is again noted.  The left kidney is
normal in size, and there is a interpolar hypodensity which is too small to
characterize but statistically likely to represent a cyst (series 2:image 60).
There is no evidence of hydronephrosis or nephrolithiasis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: Postsurgical changes from prior paraesophageal hernia repair
is noted.  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness, and
enhancement throughout.  A large fecal load is noted throughout the colon, and
there is no signs of wall thickening.  The appendix is not visualized.  There
is no evidence of mesenteric injury.

There is no free fluid or free air in the abdomen.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus is not visualized. Bilateral adnexa are within
normal limits.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm or retroperitoneal hematoma. 
Extensive atherosclerotic disease is noted.

BONES: Prior right femoral neck surgical reduction is noted.  The patient is
status post median sternotomy, and prior nondisplaced seventh through tenth
posterior right rib fractures are noted.  No acute fracture is seen.

SOFT TISSUES:  There are multiple hematomas along the left gluteal and left
lateral thigh including a 5.9 x 3.5 cm hematoma along the left lateral thigh. 
Associated soft tissue induration and edema is noted.

IMPRESSION:


1. Multiple hematomas along the left gluteal and left lateral thigh with
associated soft tissue induration.
2. Status post type A aortic dissection repair.  Further evaluation is limited
without intravenous contrast material, though the appearance is similar to
prior exam.
